interest: This docket sheet provides valuable evidence of U.S. consular surveillance and intelligence gathering regarding Japanese activities, land holdings, and potential espionage in British Columbia in the interwar/pre-WWII period. It illustrates the role of the U.S. Consulate General in Vancouver under Paul R. Josselyn in monitoring Japanese residents and strategic vulnerabilities along the Pacific Coast of Canada. For diplomatic and intelligence historians, it provides critical archival metadata—including despatch numbers, dates, and departmental routing—for tracing lost or cross-filed reports on suspected fifth-column activities and military intelligence operations.
overview: This file consists of a U.S. Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.20242H, concerning Japanese military activities, intelligence gathering, espionage, and propaganda in British Columbia, Canada. The sheet indexes three documents received from American Consul Paul R. Josselyn in Vancouver and routed to the Division of European Affairs (EU), Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE), and related departmental offices: an unnumbered report of October 7 examining the Japanese population, property holdings, and activities in British Columbia; Despatch No. 986 of December 13 transmitting additional copies of a report on the subject; and Despatch No. 1049 of January 21 transmitting copies of despatches reporting further developments.

subfiles.about: A State Department list of papers cataloguing three consular reports from Vancouver regarding Japanese population, land holdings, and military activities in British Columbia.
subfiles.summary: This document serves as the index sheet for State Department decimal file 894.20242H on Japanese military activities in British Columbia. It records an October 7 report from Consul Paul R. Josselyn detailing the Japanese problem, population, land holdings, and activities in the province. It further records Josselyn's Despatch No. 986 (December 13) and Despatch No. 1049 (January 21) transmitting related reports and despatches on subsequent developments, routed to the European Affairs and Far Eastern Affairs divisions.
